solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See me burn maybe when this calculator has done its work?

parts.note: these six letters are what a six-letter word for a figure becomes once it has been crunched, that is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is warned they will get burnt by a hard-working calculating machine once it has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue shows the result of an anagram, not its fodder: crunch NUMBER and you might see ME BURN, so the device that does the crunching is the answer. The blog calls it an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or machine that does heavy arithmetic is colloquially called this, so it fits a calculator.

clue.text: Poetic pieces with a sort of appeal from Ukrainian city

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Lyric verse with a certain charm comes out of a Black Sea port.
explanation.definitionFit: Odesa is a major port on Ukraine's Black Sea coast, often spelt with a double S in English.

clue.text: Story about resistance and disagreement

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the story word encloses the resistance letter

parts.note: fiction is a made-up story
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A tale about putting up a fight and falling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people means conflict or discord.

clue.text: A space that has its attraction

definitions.text: A space that has its attraction

parts.words: A space that has its attraction
parts.note: reads like a lovely spot, but describes a region where a lodestone exerts its pull

explanation.definitionFit: The area around a magnet in which its force acts is a region, or space, of attraction.

clue.text: Abduct small child having sleep

parts.note: a kid is a young child
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A toddler having a doze is seized by kidnappers.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to carry someone off by force, a synonym of abduct.

clue.text: Stressed-out oarsman's thrown up in lavatory

indicators.note: in places the turned oarsman inside the lavatory word

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet

indicators.note: in a down clue thrown up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rower is an oarsman; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An anxious rower has been sick in the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn describes someone worn down and haggard from worry.

clue.text: Where those who have dug up the street are progressing?

definitions.text: Where those who have dug up the street are

explanation.surface: Roadworkers in a trench are making headway.
explanation.definitionFit: Road diggers are below the road, under the way; and something under way is moving forward or in progress.

clue.text: Little female performer who is very good and very lively

parts.note: Viv is a short form of the girl's name Vivian
an ace is an expert player

explanation.surface: A petite actress who is excellent and full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivace is a musical direction meaning to play in a brisk, spirited way.

clue.text: Form of language that may convey ugly heartiness

indicators.note: the letters of the next two words may convey, i.e. be rearranged into, the dialect's name

explanation.surface: A dialect said to carry a loutish bonhomie.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTUARY ENGLISH is the accent of London and the Thames estuary, often mocked as coarse, so the anagram is also a sly comment.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variety of English speech from south-east England, blending Cockney and standard pronunciation.

clue.text: Escort rioters off — extreme Greenpeace types?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of escort rioters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Police are told to lead away the troublemakers, militant environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits Greenpeace itself does not sabotage; the definition points to radical green activists.
explanation.definitionFit: Militants who use violence or sabotage for environmental causes are known by this term.

clue.text: What could be set out in the form of ABC is?

definitions.text: What could be set out in the form of ABC is?

indicators.note: set out means arranged differently, so the five letters of ABC is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how the alphabet's start might be displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ABC of a subject is its rudiments, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ABC means the elementary, fundamental level, which is what basic describes.

clue.text: Not wanting old boxer senseless finally in one-sided fight?

indicators.note: in places the boxer and the final letter inside the word not

parts.note: taken as written
John Conteh was a British world light-heavyweight champion of the 1970s; the setter admitted the clue should have said boxer almost, dropping his final letter

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of senseless

explanation.surface: A has-been fighter knocked out at the end of a mismatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' is a link. CONTEH must lose its H, but nothing in the clue says so: on fifteensquared Bradman admitted it should have read 'boxer almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A no contest is a bout so uneven that its outcome is never in doubt.

clue.text: One who doesn't fantasise has hesitation about description of celebs

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the hesitation word is written backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A level-headed person stammers when talking about famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist faces facts rather than daydreaming.

clue.text: One old man in a bed completely rejected food

indicators.note: completely rejected means the whole assembly is turned back to front
in puts the one and the old man inside the a-plus-bed piece

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
I is the Roman numeral one
pa is father

explanation.surface: A single elderly man lying in bed refused every meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starch from cassava, eaten as a milk pudding.

clue.text: Accenting rarity? What's almost sure to happen differs from that

indicators.note: the answer differs from accenting rarity only in letter order, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about stressing the unusual, then a remark that a near-certain event is different.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing certainty is British slang for something bound to happen, like a horse sure to win.

clue.text: Class getting elected I term "almost detached"

parts.note: CL is a short form of class
a politician elected is in

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to term something is to call it

explanation.surface: A classroom description of someone in office who calls himself nearly aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinical means coldly objective and unemotional.

clue.text: An attempt to capture the core element of verse and its poetic skill

indicators.note: to capture means the a-plus-attempt pieces hold the other letters inside

parts.note: taken as written
a try is an attempt

indicators.note: core element picks the central letter of verse
poetic suggests poetic licence, so the letters of its are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying to catch the essence of poetry and its craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative ability or craftsmanship.

clue.text: Exceptional rain comes with witchcraft in African city

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters of rain are rearranged

parts.note: obi is a Caribbean form of sorcery

explanation.surface: Freak storms accompany black magic in an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

clue.text: Men to work first in Iberian city

indicators.note: first places the work word ahead of the men and to pieces

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Workers head to an Iberian port before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, a city in Portugal.

clue.text: Bunting in yellow and brown round front and back of our hospital

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

indicators.note: round means the brown word goes around the other letters

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: front picks the opening letter of our
back of picks the closing letter of hospital

explanation.surface: A small bird dressed in yellow and brown shows up around a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family, once a delicacy.

clue.text: Story introducing the German songs from Berlin?

parts.note: a story is a fib or lie
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A tale presented by a German about music from Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert; the question mark flags Berlin as an example of Germany.

clue.text: I vote in middle of room in middle of this vulgar rabble

indicators.note: the second in places the whole lot inside the central pair of this
middle of takes the central pair of letters of this
in puts the one and the vote inside the central letters of room
middle of takes the central pair of letters of room

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Someone casting a ballot amid a crowd of common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek phrase for the masses, the common people.

clue.text: Bargain stand running short around start of evening

indicators.note: around means the shortened stand goes round the other letter
running short means the stand word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stall is a market stand

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of evening

explanation.surface: A market stall low on stock near nightfall has something cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is something bought very cheaply.

clue.text: Some material tourists obtained in famous city district

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cloth bought by visitors in a well-known part of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'obtained in', which is only a link joining the hidden run to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the historic commercial quarter of Venice, around its famous bridge.

clue.text: Begins to get hold of the French actresses for minor roles?

indicators.note: to get hold of means the begins word encloses the French article

parts.note: starts means begins
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A theatre newcomer starts grabbing French actresses for bit parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun: young actresses on the rise rather than literally minor parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlets are young aspiring film actresses, often in small parts.
